summary: Frontend-only verification of Hero social-proof overlap bug fix and layout at desktop 1440x900, 1280 width, and mobile 390x844. Bug is FIXED: avatar container and adjacent text block have a 12px gap at both 1440 and 1280 widths — no horizontal overlap. All required data-testids are present and visible/hidden per breakpoint. No JS console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Hero.jsx uses shrink-0 on both the avatar wrapper (.flex.shrink-0) and each avatar img plus whitespace-nowrap on the trusted text — solid guard against the previous overlap regression.
Consider adding an explicit aria-label to the avatar images (currently alt="") for accessibility; they are decorative but a11y tools flag empty alts inconsistently.
The industries divider uses xl:block; on lg (1024–1279) the industries text wraps onto row 2 via flex-wrap, which is intentional and works well.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hero social-proof overlap bug is confirmed fixed at 1440 and 1280. Fix implemented via flex-wrap on container, shrink-0 on avatar wrapper + individual imgs, whitespace-nowrap on text. All hero data-testids working correctly across desktop and mobile.
rca of the issue: Original bug: flex children (avatars) were shrinking, causing the -space-x-2 negative margins to pull the adjacent text over the avatar images. Fix (verified): added shrink-0 to the avatar wrap container and each img, plus flex-wrap on the parent to allow the industries text to wrap to a new line at narrower widths rather than compressing avatars. Result: 12px measured gap between avatar group and text block at both 1440 and 1280 viewports.
